title: The B500 — Schwarzwaldhochstrasse, Panoramastrasse and Baden Wine
subRegion: Schwarzwald and the Baden wine terraces, Baden-Württemberg

bestPeriod.note: The B500 ridge is open all year but drifts and freezing fog close sections in midwinter; late September brings the wine harvest and the clearest air.

basecamps: Baden-Baden, Triberg and Freiburg im Breisgau
summary: The Schwarzwaldhochstrasse and Panoramastrasse driven end to end, with Baden vineyards, the Kandel hairpins and a Kaiserstuhl finish.
hook: Germany's oldest scenic road runs along a fir ridge above the Rhine plain, and on a clear evening you can see the Vosges from it. Below the ridge the same trip becomes something else entirely: hairpins into vine terraces, a wine village every eight kilometres, and cake taken seriously.

snapshot.Base(s): Baden-Baden (2 nights), Freudenstadt (1), Triberg (1), Freiburg im Breisgau (3)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 780 km; ridge roads and hairpin descents, gradients to 10%, max altitude 1,241 m
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Karlsruhe/Baden-Baden (FKB), Stuttgart (STR) or Basel (EAP); rail to Offenburg also works
snapshot.Who It Suits: Unhurried drivers, cake enthusiasts, anyone who wants scenery without altitude sickness

itinerary.title: Baden-Baden and the Ortenau terraces
itinerary.morning: Collect the car and check for a green **Umweltplakette** on the windscreen. Baden-Baden and Freiburg itself no longer run low-emission zones, but Karlsruhe still does, and the sticker is what gets you in there.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive the Badische Weinstrasse north-south through **Neuweier** and **Varnhalt**, terraced Riesling slopes where the local bottle shape is the flat-sided Bocksbeutel, then **Sasbachwalden**, half-timbered and steep. Small Winzergenossenschaft tasting rooms sit directly on the road with free parking.
itinerary.evening: Baden-Baden. Leave the car in the Kongresshaus garage and walk the Lichtentaler Allee to the Trinkhalle; the historic Friedrichsbad and the Caracalla Therme are five minutes apart.
itinerary.dayStats: 70 km · 1h40 driving · no passes · max altitude 420 m.

itinerary.title: Schwarzwaldhochstrasse
itinerary.morning: The **B500 Schwarzwaldhochstrasse** proper: 60 km from Baden-Baden to Freudenstadt, opened in 1930 and never tolled. It climbs quickly to the ridge at Sand and stays between 800 and 1,000 m the whole way, with the Rhine plain on the right and spruce on the left.
itinerary.afternoon: Stop at the **Mummelsee** (1,036 m) — a glacial tarn with a large paid car park that fills by 11:00 on summer Sundays — and walk 25 minutes up to the **Hornisgrinde**, 1,164 m, the northern Black Forest's highest point, with a boardwalk across the moor and a viewing tower. Continue to the **Nationalparkzentrum Ruhestein**, a striking stack of cantilevered timber boxes above the pass at 915 m, then **Schliffkopf** (1,055 m) and the **Kniebis** saddle (935 m).
itinerary.evening: Freudenstadt, whose market square is the largest in Germany and is essentially a car park with arcades. Free parking, which is unusual and welcome.
itinerary.dayStats: 80 km · 2h00 driving · 3 saddles (Ruhestein, Schliffkopf, Kniebis) · max altitude 1,036 m.

itinerary.title: Kinzig valley and the clock country
itinerary.morning: South on the B294 to **Alpirsbach** and its Romanesque monastery church, then **Schiltach**, a raft-builders' town of white-and-black timber houses stacked up a hillside. Park below the Marktplatz; the square itself is on a slope and cobbled.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Vogtsbauernhof** open-air museum at Gutach preserves real Black Forest farmhouses moved from across the region, including the low-slung roofs that run down to the ground. Then **Triberg**: the waterfall drops 163 m in seven cascades and charges entry; the upper Wasserfall car park saves the climb.
itinerary.evening: Stay in Triberg or Schonach. Ask your hotel for the **KONUS Gästekarte** — it makes all regional buses and trains free for overnight guests, which is worth knowing on a driving trip too.
itinerary.dayStats: 115 km · 2h30 driving · no passes · max altitude 1,000 m.

itinerary.title: Schwarzwald-Panoramastrasse and the Kandel
itinerary.morning: Join the signposted **Schwarzwald-Panoramastrasse**, a 275 km route that links the high plateaux. Take it via Furtwangen — the Deutsches Uhrenmuseum has the original cuckoo mechanisms and the world's largest clock collection — over the **Thurner** at 1,036 m to **St. Märgen** and **St. Peter**, whose Baroque abbey library is one of the finest interiors in Baden.
itinerary.afternoon: The **Kandelstrasse**: 11 km of tight, cambered hairpins from the Kandel pass at 1,241 m down to Waldkirch, with gradients to 10% and a well-earned reputation among motorcyclists. Drive it downhill in the afternoon with the Rhine plain opening ahead.
itinerary.evening: Into Freiburg im Breisgau for three nights. The city centre is largely pedestrianised (its Umweltzone was lifted in May 2025); use the Schlossberg or Rotteckring garages and walk.
itinerary.dayStats: 140 km · 3h20 driving · 2 passes (Thurner, Kandel) · max altitude 1,241 m.

itinerary.title: Schauinsland, Belchen and the Münstertal
itinerary.morning: The **Schauinslandstrasse** climbs from Horben in about 170 curves — a former hill-climb course, now speed-limited and camera-watched — to a summit car park near 1,220 m. Parking is paid; the tower is a ten-minute walk.
itinerary.afternoon: Over the **Notschrei** pass (1,121 m) and down to Todtnau, then up to Multen for the **Belchen**, 1,414 m. Private cars are banned from the last stretch to the summit: you park at Multen and take the Belchen-Seilbahn cable car or the shuttle bus. This is the region's best 360-degree view — Vosges, Jura, and the Alps on a clear autumn day.
itinerary.evening: Over the **Wiedener Eck** (1,037 m) and down through the **Münstertal** to Staufen, where the Fausthaus faces the market square, then back to Freiburg.
itinerary.dayStats: 130 km · 3h10 driving · 3 passes (Schauinsland, Notschrei, Wiedener Eck) · max altitude 1,220 m.

itinerary.title: Höllental, Feldberg and the Wutach
itinerary.morning: East on the **B31 through the Höllental**, a narrow rock gorge with the Hirschsprung statue on a ledge above the road, to **Titisee**. Then the **Feldbergpass** at 1,231 m, the highest through-road in the Black Forest, under the 1,493 m Feldberg summit.
itinerary.afternoon: Round the **Schluchsee**, then **St. Blasien**, whose enormous domed cathedral is a shock in a village of that size. Loop east to the **Wutachschlucht** gorge — the Schattenmühle car park is the standard access point for the two-hour walk in.
itinerary.evening: Return via Titisee and the Höllental. Watch for evening deer on the B500 stretches south of Hinterzarten.
itinerary.dayStats: 165 km · 3h20 driving · 1 pass (Feldbergpass) · max altitude 1,231 m.

itinerary.title: Kaiserstuhl and out
itinerary.morning: West to the **Kaiserstuhl**, a volcanic hill island in the Rhine plain planted almost entirely with vines. Drive the loess terraces via Ihringen, Achkarren and Oberbergen; the Vulkanfelsen and Badberg viewpoints look across to Alsace.
itinerary.afternoon: **Breisach** on the Rhine, with the Stephansmünster on its rock and the French bank in walking distance. Lunch, a last Spätburgunder tasting at a village cooperative, then the A5 north or south.
itinerary.evening: Drop the car. If flying from Basel's EuroAirport, note the terminal has separate French and Swiss sectors — return to the sector your contract names, since the Swiss side implies the Swiss motorway vignette.
itinerary.dayStats: 80 km · 1h50 driving · no passes · max altitude 560 m.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel am Markt
accommodationStrategy.description: A modest, long-run house on the market square by the Stiftskirche, uphill from the spa quarter and inside the old town — so the Friedrichsbad, the Trinkhalle and the Lichtentaler Allee are all walkable. Parking is arranged nearby rather than on site, which is normal in Baden-Baden's old streets.
accommodationStrategy.booking: six weeks; longer for the Iffezheim race meetings.

accommodationStrategy.name: Parkhotel Wehrle
accommodationStrategy.description: A 17th-century inn with its own park in the middle of Triberg, five minutes from the waterfall entrance and with proper on-site parking — which matters, because Triberg's centre is a narrow valley floor with very little of it. It also fixes the trip's weak spot: the middle Black Forest is short on characterful beds.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Zum Roten Bären
accommodationStrategy.description: Documented from 1120 and arguably the oldest inn in Germany, on the Oberlinden by the Schwabentor. Its garage is the practical point: Freiburg's centre is pedestrianised and crossed by tram lines and Bächle water channels, and having a parked car inside the ring for three nights is worth paying for.

logistics.emergency: 112 for everything; 110 for police. Bergwacht Schwarzwald handles gorge and forest rescues through 112.
logistics.weather: Winter tyres are legally required in winter conditions (the *situative Winterreifenpflicht*), and the B500 above 900 m gets freezing fog and drifting snow from November. Sections around Ruhestein and Schliffkopf close for hours at a time.
logistics.money: Cards are widely taken but small Winzergenossenschaften, mountain Gasthäuser and cake counters still prefer cash or Girocard. Shops shut at 20:00 and everything closes on Sunday except bakeries and petrol stations.

other.label: No car toll, but a sticker
other.text: Germany charges cars nothing for Autobahn use. What you do need is the green **Umweltplakette** for Umweltzonen — in this region Karlsruhe, Stuttgart, Mannheim and Heidelberg (Freiburg's zone was lifted in May 2025). It costs €6–€20 at TÜV, DEKRA or a workshop; German rentals normally carry one, foreign-plated cars usually do not, and the fine is charged per entry.

other.label: Cross-border
other.text: Alsace is 20 minutes from Freiburg and Basel is 60. In France you need a **Crit'Air** sticker for the Strasbourg zone; in Switzerland the motorway **Autobahnvignette** costs CHF 40 and is sold only as an annual, valid from 1 December to 31 January of the following year, now also as an e-vignette linked to the plate.

other.label: Rental restrictions
other.text: German rentals allow France, Switzerland, Austria and the Benelux as standard; eastward travel is often restricted and one-way drops abroad — Freiburg to Basel or Strasbourg — attract fees from €100. Confirm the Swiss vignette question before crossing.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 for everything; 110 for police. Bergwacht Schwarzwald handles gorge and forest rescues through 112.

other.label: Speed and cameras
other.text: The Schauinslandstrasse, the Kandel and the B500 all carry permanent speed and noise cameras, aimed mainly at motorcycles. Limits drop to 50 or 60 km/h without much warning.

proTips: Take the **KONUS Gästekarte** from any participating hotel: free regional trains and buses for overnight guests. Use it to ride up to Feldberg or Schauinsland and walk down, leaving the car behind.
Drive the Kandel and the Schauinsland downhill in late afternoon. Both face west, and both are jammed with motorcycles on Sunday mornings.
Do the Mummelsee before 10:00 or after 17:00. The car park is the bottleneck for the whole northern B500 on summer weekends.
You cannot drive up the Belchen — build in the cable car at Multen or the road is a dead end with a barrier.
Café Schäfer in Triberg still makes Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte to the documented original recipe. It is a small shop, and it sells out.
In the Kaiserstuhl, aim for a village cooperative rather than a roadside shop: Achkarren, Oberrotweil and Ihringen all pour Spätburgunder and Grauburgunder for a couple of euros a glass.
The Wutachschlucht is best walked one way with the bus back, which the KONUS card makes free.

packingNotes: Walking shoes with tread: the Wutach gorge path is rooty, wet and unimproved.
A warm layer for the ridge — Hornisgrinde in May is often 10°C colder than Baden-Baden.
Swimwear and flip-flops for the Baden-Baden thermal baths; the Friedrichsbad is textile-free, the Caracalla is not.
A cool bag for wine bought at cooperatives; car boots in the Rhine plain reach 50°C in summer.
Cash, roughly €150, for parking meters, small tastings and cake.
Insect repellent for the Wutach and the moorland boardwalks in June.
Sunglasses — the ridge road runs west-facing all afternoon.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Snow or fog shuts the B500 ridge.** Fallback: the parallel B462 and B33 through the Kinzig and Murg valleys stay open and reach the same towns; you lose the view, not the day.
**You enter Karlsruhe without an Umweltplakette.** Fallback: buy one at a TÜV or DEKRA station on the edge of the city before driving in, or park at a Park-and-Ride tram stop outside the zone.
**Sunday closures strand you without food.** Fallback: Autobahn service areas and bakery cafés open Sunday mornings; buy provisions on Saturday before 20:00.
**Motorcycle weekend traffic on the passes.** Fallback: move the Kandel, Schauinsland and Mummelsee legs to weekdays and use Saturday and Sunday for the Kaiserstuhl and the wine villages.
